值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解黃仁勳回歸 Nvidia 的背景，以及美國政府態度轉變如何影響董事會決策。
  • 看懂 Nvidia 為何難以另覓接班人，以及公司面臨的產品、訴訟與政治壓力。
  • 認識黃仁勳復任後新增的合規監督安排，並思考這些制度能否真正制衡創辦人權力。

摘要

黃仁勳回歸與董事會轉向

作者指出，黃仁勳重返 Nvidia 出乎許多人意料。先前董事會曾表示不會讓他回任，並以個人行為不符合公司標準與文化為由將他撤換；然而，在他回歸的消息傳出後，董事會態度急轉。作者認為，代理執行長在財報電話會議上避談黃仁勳的貢獻與離職，只聚焦營運數據、安撫員工，甚至宣布加薪，卻難以消除市場與人才對公司前景的疑慮。

美國政府態度改變，政治阻力消退

作者將黃仁勳回歸的重要推力，歸因於美國政府立場的轉變。美國財政部長貝森特起初主張 Nvidia 應從外部尋找新執行長，後來卻改口稱黃仁勳已離職，因此也可視為外部人選。作者提到，川普公開要求董事會重新聘用黃仁勳，貝森特隨後改變說法；在政府官員表態支持、並認定黃仁勳不構成國安風險後，董事會最大的政治顧慮也隨之減弱。

接班人難尋，公司正值關鍵時刻

作者認為，董事會選擇黃仁勳，也因為「如果不是他，還能找誰」。Nvidia 曾委託獵頭公司尋找接班人，但被視為合適人選的 Arm 執行長 Rene Haas 隨後與 SoftBank 簽下長約，並婉拒相關可能。Nvidia 的競爭力不只在硬體，也仰賴龐大複雜的軟體生態系、供應鏈與客戶關係；外部人選需要時間理解公司運作，內部人選則未必具備領導整家公司所需的商業、政治與供應鏈能力。

新任執行長還得立即面對中國晶片出貨調查、股東集體訴訟，以及國會聽證等挑戰，幾乎沒有適應期。與此同時，Nvidia 正忙於向 Google Cloud、Azure 與 Oracle 推進新一代 Blackwell、Rubin 系統，也須應對科技巨頭自研晶片的競爭。作者指出，若領導交接造成猶豫，競爭者便可能趁機追趕，因此這個燙手山芋最終仍得由熟悉公司全局的黃仁勳接手。

市場反應與回任的條件

作者認為，市場對「後黃仁勳時代」的恐慌超出董事會預期。董事會最後以股東、員工、合作夥伴與客戶的利益為由，支持他復任；消息公布後，Nvidia 股價在星期一上漲超過三成，也帶動其他 AI 與科技股。作者以此指出，市場用股價展現黃仁勳對公司的重要性，即使部分主流媒體曾批評他，他的價值仍難以取代。

不過，作者強調黃仁勳回歸並非毫無限制。Nvidia 將設立新的首席合規官（CCO），負責監督全公司的法規遵循，並直接向董事會提名與公司治理委員會報告，而非向黃仁勳負責。若涉及出口管制疑慮，合規官可繞過執行長，直接向獨立董事提出報告。作者將此安排形容為制衡黃仁勳、安撫華府與華爾街的防火牆，但也質疑，在黃仁勳仍是公司核心靈魂的情況下，這個職位是否真有能力約束他。

權力制衡與未來考驗

除了設立 CCO，董事會也成立國家安全與出口管制委員會，並讓獨立董事長 Tench 留任，以推動權力分立。作者提醒，黃仁勳復任並不代表相關調查就此結束；他預期，隔年一月民主黨正式掌握國會兩院後，將成為黃仁勳面臨的重要考驗。整體而言，公司的制度設計試圖將技術、產品與業務交由黃仁勳負責，而出口與國安審查則交給合規官及獨立董事會監督；但這套制度能否在商業利益與強勢創辦人面前真正發揮作用，仍有待時間驗證。作者最後邀請觀眾持續關注後續發展。

================================================

You know what? I'm not. >> Lao Huang is back. Unexpected, right? Surprised? After Trump’s trip to Shenzhen, the Nvidia board’s attitude did a complete 180-degree turn. I don’t know if the two are related, but everyone knows that before this, Chairman Qiong Shi firmly stated that he wouldn’t let Lao Huang return. Even though Lao Huang had already apologized and humbly stated that he would be willing to return if the board felt it was in everyone's best interest , they publicly claimed he was let go because his personal conduct didn't align with company standards and culture , and thus wouldn't let him back. They really shut the door—don't take us for fools, okay? Lao Huang was ousted by your board, he didn't leave voluntarily. Okay, now that he’s back, Qiong Shi is embarrassed, and while interim CEO Chris didn’t directly criticize or belittle Lao Huang, he effectively played along with the board’s "de-Huang-ization" during the earnings call. He completely avoided discussing Lao Huang’s contributions and departure, focusing entirely on business data and. stabilizing morale. He threw out news of employee raises to try and steady their nerves. He finished by saying "we’ve got this," but the whole world knows he doesn't. No one is going to believe a CFO acting as CEO of a top tech firm when he says, "we’ve got this." If Lao Huang hadn't come back, maybe all of Nvidia’s top talent would have been poached by competitors—what "got this" would be left?

Nvidia’s struggling stock price should be enough to prove my point, and Treasury Secretary Bessent’s change of tune earlier also foreshadowed this event. Bessent initially insisted that Nvidia must find a new CEO from outside the company. But facing a sharp drop in U.S. stocks and Trump’s explicit support, he changed his story in subsequent interviews, claiming that since Lao Huang resigned, he counts as an outsider. This way of changing his tune is truly. something, and it’s one of the main reasons for Lao Huang’s triumphant return: the U.S. government’s dramatic shift in attitude. Originally, the biggest obstacle blocking Lao Huang’s return was the U.S. government. But this situation underwent a drastic change over the past weekend. On Sunday night, Trump publicly called on the board to rehire Lao Huang, and then Bessent followed suit with his change of stance. As the wind direction shifted, whether by force or by choice. The Nvidia board finally heeded the. advice of top U.S. government officials and confirmed that Lao Huang does not pose a national security risk. Once the political red light turned green, the board’s biggest concern vanished. Regarding Lao Huang’s reinstatement, Trump even posted that it was a correct and appropriate decision. With all the pieces in place, Jensen Huang has no choice but to make a comeback. The second reason he must return is: if. not him, then who? Hiring an outsider is easy to suggest, but failure is inevitable. It is also a fact that no one can handle such a scorching hot potato. Nvidia has certainly tried to find a successor. They hired headhunter Heidrick& Struggles to search globally, and ARM CEO Rene Haas was the only candidate who could meet all the criteria.

Once the news leaked, SoftBank quickly intervened, signing Haas to a long-term contract until 2033 and appointing him Vice Chairman of the group starting December 1st. Faced with such an offer, Haas publicly praised Jensen as a legend while politely signaling he had no intention of taking the job. With their top candidate out of the running, Nvidia basically has no one. left to choose from outside. You must realize Nvidia’s moat isn’t just hardware; it’s an incredibly vast and complex software ecosystem. Combined with Jensen’s unique flat organizational structure, an outsider would likely spend quarters just trying to grasp the internal R&D and supply chain dynamics. Setting aside the shareholders, even the board of directors wouldn't approve such. a move. If an outsider won't work, what about promoting from within? That’s also largely unfeasible; CFO Colette Kress's brief time as interim left many doubting she could handle the top spot. As for the highly respected Jeff Herbst , while his technical prestige is immense, being Nvidia's CEO requires more than just tech—it demands connections, supply chain mastery, client relations, and political savvy. I’ve analyzed this in previous episodes , so I won't repeat it here. But what I haven’t mentioned is that any internal successor would immediately face a series of high-stakes challenges . Starting with the investigation into chip shipments to China. There are also class-action shareholder lawsuits and the congressional hearing set for December 1st. A new CEO would have no honeymoon period.

. Beyond this, there is another hurdle Nvidia cannot afford to fail: products. Nvidia is currently in a critical phase of shipping its next-gen Blackwell and Rubin systems to Google Cloud, Azure, and Oracle. Meanwhile, Nvidia must also defend against the encroaching threat of custom chips developed by other tech giants. Any hesitation or strategic wavering during this leadership transition could easily allow competitors to seize the. opportunity, and Nvidia’s success might well be squandered by this new CEO. A hot potato of this magnitude has to be handled by the veteran himself. After all, the one who tied the knot must be the one to untie it. When the ideal external candidate is locked out, and internal candidates are constrained by politics and technical divisions. At this point, the board of directors really doesn't have many choices left. Dragging it out any longer would mean certain death; that is why once the U.S. government gave the green light, the board immediately followed the trend, choosing the option with the lowest risk and the most direct market reaction. Let the veteran king return. It doesn't matter if the board loses face; the bottom line is what matters most. Of course, the market's panic regarding the post-Jensen era exceeded the board's expectations; they may have anticipated some volatility in Nvidia's stock price . But they likely didn't foresee such a. violent shock. That is why the board stated directly that reinstating Jensen is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, partners, and customers. Upon Jensen's return, Nvidia's stock price soared by over 30%on Monday. It gave a shot in the arm to other AI and tech stocks, and naturally, many short-sellers were wiped out—hopefully, you weren't one of them.

Mainstream media like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times spent this entire time criticizing and belittling Jensen. In the end, the market used real money to prove the irreplaceability of Jensen Huang's value. As for whether the fans of Pichai still feel bitter, perhaps only The New York Times would be interested. Of course, Jensen's return is not unconditional; first, Nvidia will establish a brand-new position: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO). This newly created role is responsible for overseeing all regulatory compliance matters across Nvidia. This CCO does not report to Jensen, but directly to the board’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee; simply put, the CCO doesn't answer to Jensen— he can't fire him, dock his pay, or suppress his reports. If Jensen wants to skirt export controls , the CCO can bypass him and slap the report directly onto the independent. directors 'desks. As CEO, Jensen's job is to drive performance and sell chips globally; that is his duty. And the CCO is there to hit the brakes; frankly, this person is there to keep Jensen in check, acting as a hostage clause to appease Wall Street and Washington. The whole world knows that at Nvidia, Jensen is god. Beyond the fact that he can do whatever he wants, his technical and commercial prestige and status are, quite simply,. unchallenged by anyone. And the CCO is a role that is institutionally completely independent of Jensen. It will prove to the outside world that even if the founder makes a triumphant return, there is still a firewall within the company that he cannot touch, keeping an eye on him. However, let's not be too naive. Even though the CCO doesn't report to Jensen on paper, it doesn't mean they can manage him in reality. After all, the soul and prestige of.

Nvidia rest entirely with Jensen; who is this CCO anyway? As for the future, will this CCO be a "tightening headband" that truly provides checks and balances, or will they be reduced to a rubber stamp for appeasing Washington regulators? That depends on who ultimately dares to take on this position that is bound to offend people, especially Jensen. No one has taken it yet. Furthermore, Nvidia's board has also established a National Security and Export Control Committee, which is also responsible for overseeing. trade regulations and national security risks. Additionally, Tench will remain as independent chairman to provide checks and balances on Jensen's power and implement a separation of powers. Most importantly, Jensen's return does not mean the investigations against him are over. Next January, after the Democrats officially take control of both houses, that will be the true test for Jensen. In short, Nvidia has now split Jensen's power in half. Technology, products, and. business are left to Jensen. Export and national security reviews are left to the CCO and the independent board. This institutional design looks perfect on paper, but when the company faces huge commercial interests again, can this system really stand up to a powerful founder and greedy shareholders ? That is where it gets truly interesting . In time, we will know the answer. Know a little about everything, and life. becomes more colorful. See you next time.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TlkXpPHqGbo

值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解作者如何質疑《紐約時報》等媒體對黃仁勳管理風格的報導與匿名消息來源。
  • 認識高壓管理、企業表現與員工離職率之間的討論，並思考領導者的強勢風格是否必然代表職場文化有問題。
  • 看見媒體評價如何隨企業領導人的聲勢起落而轉變，以及匿名爆料可能帶來的查證與立場疑慮。

摘要

匿名指控與媒體報導

作者談到，《紐約時報》在黃仁勳宣布辭職後，接連刊出批評文章，將他的管理風格形容為傲慢、自負且難以容忍異議，並引述消息人士描述他在會議中對高管發怒、摔水瓶，造成員工不敢發言的文化。作者質疑，這些說法多出自匿名人士，缺少公開錄音或影像等資料佐證，因此讀者難以獨立查證。

高壓領導與企業文化

作者提到，黃仁勳曾以「台灣父母式的嚴厲批判」形容自己的管理方式，並將其目的說成追求卓越，而非懲罰員工。作者也以輝達約2.5%的離職率作為參照，質疑這是否符合外界所描繪的有毒職場文化；同時舉穆里尼奧、馬斯克與賈伯斯等人為例，指出一些追求極致成果的領導者，往往採取強勢且高要求的方式。

匿名消息與媒體立場

作者進一步談及媒體對黃仁勳私人感情生活的報導，指出相關婚外情說法也仰賴匿名消息，部分細節甚至未能確認。作者認為，媒體若過度依賴匿名爆料，可能讓消息來源與報導立場難以檢視，也容易形成單一敘事；相較之下，社群上也有不少具名員工公開表達對黃仁勳的感謝。

評價轉變與事件疑雲

作者認為，當輝達股價上漲時，黃仁勳的管理方式常被稱為有遠見；當風向轉變，類似特質卻可能被重新描述為傲慢自負，呈現出媒體「見高就拜、見低就踩」的現象。至於私人感情問題，作者主張應由當事人的家人處理，而不該只憑輿論定論。最後，作者指出這些消息的來源與動機仍不明，並猜測事件可能牽涉政治與企業內幕，但表示相關判斷仍待更多資料釐清。

=============

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TlkXpPHqGbo

老黃辭職後，《紐約時報》連續兩天刊出「觀點」文章，把輝達內部文化與老黃的管理風格直接定性為傲慢自負、無法容忍異議。然而這些指控幾乎全來自匿名知情人士，至今沒有任何公開錄音或影像可驗證，就連離職率也無法印證這一點。當一家市值數兆美元的公司領導人突然墜落，媒體的鞭屍與匿名指控，究竟還原了多少真相，又隱藏了多少立場？

值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解影片如何分析創辦人持股與公司治理結構，為何可能影響執行長的去留。
  • 比較英特爾、波音與麥當勞的執行長更替案例，思考不同企業對領導者的依賴程度。
  • 掌握作者對輝達接班、技術方向及美中晶片關係的擔憂與推測。

摘要

風波擴大與創辦人去留

作者回顧自己先前的看法：單一婚外情未必足以撼動輝達或迫使黃仁勳離職。然而，影片聲稱相關傳聞已不只一樁，而是牽涉多名女性，情勢因此出現變化；作者推測，若風波持續擴大，黃仁勳即使不願離開，也可能難以留任。作者也提到外界對輝達市值下滑的說法，並將其與事件發展相連結。

股權結構與董事會權力

作者指出，輝達採用單一類別普通股，黃仁勳持股約百分之三點五八，沒有超級投票權；相較之下，馬克．祖克柏透過雙重股權結構掌握較大的投票權。依作者的說法，輝達董事會十一名成員中，只要六人支持罷免，黃仁勳便可能失去職位。作者認為，這種治理結構曾被視為透明、符合現代企業標準，但也意味著創辦人較難在董事會決定時保住職位。

美中晶片政策的影響

作者認為，黃仁勳一直積極遊說美國政府放寬對中國出口先進人工智慧晶片的限制，並曾爭取出售 H20、H200 等晶片。作者轉述其策略考量：藉由讓中國持續使用美國技術標準，延緩中國發展替代方案，同時維持輝達在中國市場的收益。作者推測，黃仁勳離開後，美中之間可能出現短期溝通真空，而美國國會限制對中晶片出口的聲音或因此更強；另一方面，這也可能促使中國加快自主研發。

其他企業案例與接班風險

影片回顧波音、惠普、英特爾與麥當勞等公司曾發生高層因私人關係或違反規範而離職的案例。作者認為，波音與麥當勞的營運較依賴既有工程體系、供應鏈與標準化模式，因此領導人更替未必會根本改變企業方向；但輝達更像是由黃仁勳的技術判斷與個人願景深刻塑造的公司。

英特爾經驗與輝達的技術方向

作者將輝達目前由財務長柯蕾特．克瑞斯暫代執行長，與英特爾過去由財務背景的鮑勃．史旺接任相提並論。作者認為，史旺任內英特爾的技術路線與執行仍顯混亂，並在人工智慧與 GPU 領域落後；雖然英特爾的困境不能全歸咎於他，但這段經驗讓作者擔心，若輝達由缺乏工程背景的管理者掌舵，公司會否也逐漸偏重財務考量，而削弱技術領導力。

接班人選與黃仁勳是否回歸

作者提出另一種可能：由參與 CUDA 發展的工程師伊恩．巴克接任，但也質疑他能否延續黃仁勳多年來所建立的技術願景、說服力與國際關係。作者認為，輝達與投資人已高度依賴黃仁勳的判斷，因此接班者面臨的挑戰不只是維持營運，更是延續公司的技術與決策文化。最後，作者認為黃仁勳像史蒂夫．賈伯斯或山姆．奧特曼那樣回歸的可能性不高，並以期待他與馬斯克建立合作關係作為結尾。

But as a co-founder, why was it so easy for Jensen to be kicked out? Simply put, Nvidia uses a single-class common stock structure—no dual-class shares, no A/B shares. let go after his affair with a subordinate, it had little impact on Boeing's overall operations, as the company’s technology and projects rely heavily on engineering systems and structure. The same goes for McDonald's CEO Easterbrook; although he was single at the time and it wasn't an extramarital affair, he had relations with multiple subordinates and granted them stock options as perks, severely violating company policy and regulations. So, he was eventually fired by the board , but McDonald's is just McDonald's. It sells burgers and fries, and its business model is highly standardized franchising. Its core competitiveness lies in operational efficiency, supply chain, and brand—it doesn't require a specific CEO's technical vision. Therefore, after the new CEO took office , McDonald's overall strategy continued , and its performance and stock price recovered steadily with no major impact .

A more comparable example should be Intel, where former CEO Krzanich also resigned due to an affair. He joined Intel in 1982 as an engineer, working his way up to COO before eventually becoming CEO. During his tenure, Intel had already begun to show signs of falling behind, losing its process manufacturing lead to TSMC. After he stepped down, the company appointed then-CFO Bob Swan as interim CEO, which is exactly the same approach. Nvidia is taking now by having CFO Colette Kress serve as interim CEO. What’s even more similar is that both Swan and Kress are "firefighters" with purely financial backgrounds. Both of them lack an engineer's DNA. Although Intel was already on the decline when Swan took over, the fault doesn't lie entirely with him, but rather with a series of strategic errors by his two predecessors, such as refusing to manufacture chips for the original iPhone. However, having someone with no.

technical background like Swan serve as CEO for two years surely contributed to the continued confusion in Intel’s technical roadmap and execution. They were slow to react in the fields of AI and GPUs. This led to Intel falling behind its competitors in the AI era. Actually, Swan didn't want to be CEO at the time; he was pushed into the role by the board, but I won't go into those details here. Looking back at that period of Intel's leadership, it accelerated their. transition from a technological hegemon to a passive pursuer, missing out on the entire AI era. So, what many people are concerned about isn't how many spies or subordinates Jensen Huang may have slept with, but rather: if Nvidia's board eventually installs Colette Kress, will Nvidia follow in Intel's footsteps? Will Nvidia start prioritizing financial thinking over technology? If it’s not Kress, then who could it be ? Ian Buck? CUDA is indeed his contribution, and he.

is a world-class engineer. But for the past 33 years, Nvidia has been running on a model driven by Jensen’s technology and personal vision . Nvidia was able to bet on GPU-accelerated AI years ago, and the company and investors have grown highly dependent on Jensen’s personal judgment and powers of persuasion—not to mention his relationships with world leaders. Can Buck achieve that? Well, regardless, you had better not. expect Jensen to make a comeback at Nvidia one day. The scenes of Jobs back in the day or Sam Altman returning to OpenAI in 2023 are unlikely to happen to Jensen, because those two cases didn't involve national security, no spies were involved, and they didn't have affairs with subordinates, so their return as kings was no problem. As for Jensen, it is highly probable that he cannot go back, nor will he be coming back. Instead of dreaming of his triumphant return, it would be better to.

hope for a strong partnership between him and Musk; at least that would have a higher probability of happening. Know a little bit of everything, and life becomes more colorful. See you in the next episode.
